chunks.text:
For young adults who want an extended holiday and to work here to fund it.

Basic Eligibility
- Must be 18 to 30 years old (or 35 years old for some countries)
- Must have a passport from an eligible country or jurisdiction
- Must not be accompanied by dependent children

First Working Holiday visa
- You can work while you are here
- You can apply for a second Working Holiday visa if you meet certain eligibility criteria
Stay: 12 months. Cost: AUD840.00.

Second Working Holiday visa
- For people who currently hold, or have held, a Working Holiday visa
- You can do any kind of work while you are here
- You must have completed 3 months of specified subclass 417 work
- If in Australia, must hold a substantive visa or last substantive visa expired less than 28 days ago
- You can apply for a third Working Holiday visa if you meet certain eligibility criteria
Stay: 12 months. Cost: AUD1,000.00.

Third Working Holiday visa
- For people who currently hold, or have held, a second Working Holiday visa
- You can do any kind of work while you are here
- You must have completed 6 months of specified subclass 417 work
- If in Australia, must hold a substantive visa or last substantive visa expired less than 28 days ago
Stay: 12 months. Cost: AUD1,000.00.

Note: All subclass 417 holders are also subject to visa condition 8547 — the 6-month work limitation with the same employer (see the WHM 6 month work limitation document) — unless an exemption applies. This is a categorically different work restriction from the Subclass 500 Student visa's 48-hours-per-fortnight cap; a 417 holder can work unlimited hours but must generally rotate employer/location every 6 months, whereas a 500 holder has no employer limit but is capped at 48 hours per fortnight while their course is in session.
This temporary visa lets an employer sponsor a suitably skilled worker to fill a position they can't find a suitably skilled Australian to fill. It is employer-sponsored, not a study-pathway visa.

Basic Eligibility

You must:
- be nominated for a skilled position by an approved sponsor
- have the right skills to do the job
- meet the relevant English language requirements

Core Skills stream
Employers address labour shortages by bringing in skilled workers where they can't source an appropriately skilled Australian worker. Occupation must be on the Core Skills Occupation List.
Stay: Up to 4 years (Hong Kong passport holders up to 5 years).
Cost: From AUD4,015.00 (concessions apply in limited circumstances).

Specialist Skills stream
Occupation must be an ANZSCO occupation in Major Groups 1, 2, 4, 5 or 6, with nominated salary meeting the Specialist Skills Income Threshold.
Stay: Up to 4 years (Hong Kong passport holders up to 5 years).
Cost: From AUD4,015.00 (concessions apply in limited circumstances).

Labour agreement stream
For skilled workers nominated by employers who have a Labour Agreement in effect with the Australian Government.
Stay: Up to a maximum of 4 years, depending on the terms of the labour agreement (Hong Kong passport holders up to 5 years).
Cost: From AUD4,015.00 (concessions apply in limited circumstances).

Subsequent entrant
For family members of subclass 457 and subclass 482 visa holders joining the primary visa holder in Australia, applying separately.
Stay: As long as the visa is valid.
Cost: From AUD4,015.00 (concessions apply in limited circumstances).

Note: Subclass 482 is employer-sponsored and tied to the nominated position — it is a fundamentally different category from the Subclass 500 Student visa (course-based, 48 hours/fortnight cap while course is in session) and the Subclass 485 Temporary Graduate visa (post-study work rights, no employer sponsorship required). Work rights under 482 are attached to the sponsoring employer and nominated occupation, not a fortnightly hour cap.

Subclass 485

Temporary Graduate visa

A temporary visa that allows international students to live, study and work after you have finished your studies.

Basic Eligibility

You must:
- be aged 35 years or under when you apply (exceptions apply)
- hold an eligible visa
- have held a Student visa in the last 6 months
- have a recent qualification in a CRICOS-registered course
- apply for your eligible stream (it is not possible to change streams after you apply)
- attach required evidence when you apply

Post-Vocational Education Work stream
For international students who have recently graduated with an associate degree, diploma or trade qualification relevant to an occupation Australia needs.
- You can work in Australia (no hours restriction stated for this stream)
- You can bring your family with you
- Must hold a qualification relevant to the nominated occupation on the skilled occupation list
Stay: Up to 18 months. Hong Kong and British National Overseas passport holders may stay for 5 years.
Cost: From AUD5,750.00 (concessions apply in limited circumstances).

Post-Higher Education Work stream
For international students who have recently graduated with a degree from an Australian institution.
- You can work in Australia (no hours restriction stated for this stream)
- You can bring your family with you
- Need a recent degree in a CRICOS-registered course
Stay: Usually between 2 and 3 years, depending on qualification. Hong Kong and British National Overseas passport holders may stay for 5 years.
Cost: From AUD5,750.00 (concessions apply in limited circumstances).

Second Post-Higher Education Work stream
For Temporary Graduates holding a Post-Higher Education Work, Post-Study Work or Replacement visa with a degree from an Australian institution located in a regional area.
- You can work in Australia (no hours restriction stated for this stream)
- You can bring your family with you
Stay: Between 1 and 2 years depending on the regional location of the graduating institution and the regional area lived in while holding the visa.
Cost: From AUD2,265.00 (concessions apply in limited circumstances).

Note: Unlike the Subclass 500 Student visa (which caps work at 48 hours per fortnight while a course is in session), the Subclass 485 Temporary Graduate visa streams listed here do not carry a stated fortnightly work-hour cap — holders can work in Australia under their stream conditions. Always check the visa grant notice / VEVO for the specific conditions attached to an individual grant.

Subclass 500

Student visa

Visit Australia to participate in a course of study.

Stay
Up to 6 years and in line with your enrolment.

Cost
From AUD2,500.00 (concessions apply in limited circumstances). A lower visa cost applies to eligible Pacific Island and Timor-Leste citizens, eligible ASEAN citizens and applicants in the ELICOS and Non-Award sector who lodge a valid Student visa application.

With this visa you can
- participate in an eligible course of study in Australia
- travel in and out of Australia
- work up to 48 hours a fortnight when your course of study or training is in session.

Check your eligibility

You must:
- apply online in or outside Australia
- be enrolled in a course of study in Australia and hold a valid Confirmation of Enrolment (CoE) when the visa is decided
- hold Overseas Student Health Cover (OSHC), or fall in one of the exemption categories
- be 6 years or older
- prove you have a welfare arrangement, if you are under 18
- if in Australia, hold an eligible substantive visa

Note:
- A CoE is no longer valid if it is cancelled or the course is complete
- A substantive visa ceases to be in effect if another substantive visa is granted

chunks.subclass_label: Condition 8547 — WHM 6 month work limitation (Subclass 417 and 462)
chunks.text: Visa condition 8547 applies to anyone in Australia who holds any kind of Working Holiday Maker (WHM) visa — this includes Subclass 417 (Working Holiday) and Subclass 462 (Work and Holiday) — regardless of when they arrive. It also applies to anyone who holds a Bridging visa with condition 8547 imposed. It applies to any type of work (full time, part time, casual, shift or voluntary) unless an exemption applies.

chunks.subclass_label: Condition 8547 — WHM 6 month work limitation (Subclass 417 and 462)
chunks.text:
Exemptions to condition 8547 (from 1 January 2024, you can work for the same employer for more than 6 months WITHOUT asking permission if you work in):
- different locations for the same employer, as long as work in any one location does not exceed 6 months (e.g. two hotels in the same chain, independently-owned franchises, different school/health facilities, self-employed providing services to the same business alongside other clients)
- plant and animal cultivation anywhere in Australia (e.g. harvesting/packing crops, pruning, maintaining animals for sale, processing animal/plant products)
- natural disaster recovery work anywhere in Australia
- critical sectors anywhere in Australia: agriculture, health, aged and disability care, childcare, tourism and hospitality
- certain industries in Northern Australia only: fishing and pearling, tree farming and felling, construction, mining

chunks.subclass_label: Condition 8547 — WHM 6 month work limitation (Subclass 417 and 462)
chunks.text: If work does not fall within an exemption, you can only work for the same employer for a maximum of 6 months while holding a WHM visa.

chunks.subclass_label: Condition 8547 — WHM 6 month work limitation (Subclass 417 and 462)
chunks.text:
Requesting permission to work longer than 6 months

You may be given permission if you:
- have applied for a visa allowing ongoing full-time work and are awaiting the outcome, or
- undertake work critical to your employer, with a supporting letter attached to the request
Apply via the online form "Permission to work longer than 6 months". You can continue working while awaiting a written decision, provided the request was submitted before the 6-month period ended. If submitted after the 6 months ended, you must stop working for that employer until a decision is made.

Meaning of "same employer": the business or organisation you are directly working for. You cannot stay in the same position/location with the same employer for more than 6 months by rotating through different employment agencies, business affiliates, or sub-contracting arrangements. Workplace-based training counts as work.

chunks.subclass_label: Condition 8547 — WHM 6 month work limitation (Subclass 417 and 462)
chunks.text:
Self-employment: your "employer" for condition 8547 purposes is the end user you provide services to. You must not provide services to the same end user for longer than 6 months unless an exemption applies or written approval has been obtained — unless that end user is not your only client.

Calculating the 6 months: starts from the day you start work (full-time, part-time, casual, shift or voluntary). It is based on elapsed months, not hours or days worked. The condition applies to each visa separately — the 6-month limit restarts when a new WHM visa is granted, or when a bridging visa with condition 8547 starts.

Note: this 6-month same-employer limitation is specific to Subclass 417 and 462 WHM visas. It does NOT apply to Subclass 500 (Student), 485 (Temporary Graduate) or 482 (Skills in Demand) visas, which have their own distinct work conditions.
